The split is the four moves of the method (set up the form · clear the denominators · find the constants · write the result), one mark each, and the SAME split and the SAME step ids (s1_form, s2_identity, s3_constants, s4_result) are used on all fifteen cards of this unit, deliberately: they are one method over different fractions. For the improper fractions the division lives inside s1_form, and for the (x − 3)³ question the substitution x − 3 = y takes the place of the form. The book's SAQ chapter header carries ★★★ and reads '4 Marks'; that star is the CHAPTER's rank, not this question's. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Model Paper 3 (book p.115) asks exactly this question at Q15. No two-book check and no board back-test exist for this paper — recorded, not hidden. Truth check: putting x = 1 in the identity gives −2 = A(2) + (B + C)(3) = 2/5 + (4/5 − 8/5)(3) = 2/5 − 12/5 = −2 with A = 1/5, B = 4/5, C = −8/5.

recall_prompt: Say how you would resolve (x² − 3)/((x + 2)(x² + 1)) into partial fractions — name each move in order.
insider_note: x² + 1 does not factorise, so it takes Bx + C on top, not a constant; all three constants come out as fifths — A = 1/5, B = 4/5, C = −8/5 — and they stay as fractions to the end.

steps.label: Set up the form
steps.margin_note: First mark. x² + 1 has no real factors, so it gets Bx + C. The linear factor (x + 2) gets A. Do not confuse x² + 1 with x² − 1, which does factorise.

recall.must_convey: That x² + 1 is irreducible and the form is A/(x + 2) + (Bx + C)/(x² + 1).
accept: x squared plus one cannot be factorised so write A over x plus two plus Bx plus C over x squared plus one
linear factor gets A and the quadratic gets Bx plus C
A by x plus 2 plus Bx plus C by x square plus 1
x square plus one ki real factors levu, kabatti A by x plus two plus Bx plus C by x square plus one ani rasali
the irreducible quadratic needs a linear numerator

steps.why: Over an irreducible quadratic the numerator must be linear, Bx + C, so the identity has enough unknowns to match the x², x and constant terms. This is the same form as (2x² + 3x + 4)/((x − 1)(x² + 2)) with different numbers.
common_mistakes: Factorising x² + 1 as (x + 1)(x − 1); that is x² − 1.
Writing the numerator x² − 3 as (x + √3)(x − √3) and trying to cancel; nothing cancels.

steps.label: Clear the denominators
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Multiply by (x + 2)(x² + 1). A keeps (x² + 1), (Bx + C) keeps (x + 2).

recall.must_convey: That multiplying through gives x² − 3 = A(x² + 1) + (Bx + C)(x + 2).
accept: multiply both sides by x plus two into x squared plus one to get x squared minus three equals A into x squared plus one plus Bx plus C into x plus two
clear the denominators so A keeps x squared plus one and Bx plus C keeps x plus two
multiply through by the whole denominator to get an identity in x
denominator tho multiply cheste A into x square plus one plus Bx plus C into x plus two vastundi
remove the fractions by multiplying with x plus two times x squared plus one
heard_as: A into x squared plus one
Bx plus C into x plus two

steps.why: The polynomial identity is where the constants are found. Both sides are quadratics, so one root and two coefficient comparisons determine A, B and C.
common_mistakes: Writing Bx + C(x + 2) without the bracket.
Giving A the factor (x + 2) instead of (x² + 1).

steps.label: Find the constants
steps.margin_note: Third mark. x = −2 gives A = 1/5. x = 0 gives A + 2C = −3, so C = −8/5. Compare x² for B = 4/5. Fractions with 5 all the way; keep them as fractions.

recall.must_convey: That x = −2 gives A = 1/5, x = 0 gives A + 2C = −3 so C = −8/5, and comparing x² gives A + B = 1 so B = 4/5.
accept: put x equals minus two to get A equals one by five, x equals zero to get A plus two C equals minus three so C is minus eight by five, compare x squared to get B equals four by five
A is one fifth from the root, C is minus eight fifths from x equals zero and B is four fifths from the x squared coefficient
A one by five, C minus eight by five, B four by five
x equals minus two pedithe A one by five, x equals zero pedithe C minus eight by five, x square compare cheste B four by five
one root, x equals zero and the x squared coefficient give the three constants

steps.why: The root of the linear factor gives A. x = 0 is the easiest non-root value because Bx vanishes and only A and C remain. B then follows from the x² coefficient A + B = 1.
common_mistakes: Putting x = −2 and writing (−2)² − 3 as −7 instead of 1.
Solving A + 2C = −3 as C = (−3 − A)/2 with A = 1/5 and getting −7/5; −3 − 1/5 = −16/5, half of that is −8/5.
Writing B = 1 by forgetting A in the x² coefficient.

steps.label: Write the result
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Bx + C = (4/5)x − 8/5 = (4x − 8)/5, so the second fraction is (4x − 8)/(5(x² + 1)). The first is 1/(5(x + 2)).

steps.why: Fractional constants are presented with the denominator 5 moved under the bracket. This keeps each term on one line and is the form the book and the examiner expect.
common_mistakes: Not checking: put x = 1 in the identity, −2 = 2/5 − 12/5. If the two sides differ, a constant is wrong.
